readings: For each event in the budget table (`budget.link_to_event`), work out the average budgeted `amount` across its budget lines, ignoring missing amounts. Take the overall average as the mean of these per-event averages, with each event counting once, and keep only the events whose average is above it. For each such event, show the event link, its average amount, how far that is above the overall average, and its average minus the mean of the kept events' averages. Sort by this last difference, largest first, and show the top 10.
queries:
WITH per_event AS (
    SELECT link_to_event, AVG(amount) AS average_amount
    FROM budget
    GROUP BY link_to_event
),
overall AS (
    SELECT AVG(average_amount) AS overall_average
    FROM per_event
),
kept AS (
    SELECT p.link_to_event, p.average_amount, o.overall_average
    FROM per_event AS p
    CROSS JOIN overall AS o
    WHERE p.average_amount > o.overall_average
),
kept_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(average_amount) AS mean_average
    FROM kept
)
SELECT
    k.link_to_event,
    k.average_amount,
    k.average_amount - k.overall_average AS above_overall_average,
    k.average_amount - m.mean_average AS difference_from_kept_mean
FROM kept AS k
CROSS JOIN kept_mean AS m
ORDER BY difference_from_kept_mean DESC
LIMIT 10
